entry.title: Cornell President Kotlikoff’s 2026 State of the University Address at the Joint Annual Meeting

media:group.media:title: Cornell President Kotlikoff’s 2026 State of the University Address at the Joint Annual Meeting
media:group.media:description:
On October 15, 2026, President Michael I. Kotlikoff delivered his State of the University address at the Cornell University Board of Trustees and University Council Joint Annual Meeting (part of the Volunteer Summit) in the new Meinig Fieldhouse.
In the address, he discusses recent events that have deeply affected the Cornell community and the university’s responsibility to support and care for its members. He outlines the beginning of a sustained, community-wide effort that includes a thorough review of campus practices and structures, and he expresses gratitude to and concern for those who have come forward to share their experiences.
President Kotlikoff also reflects on Cornell’s 161-year mission of education, research, and public impact, while addressing the broader challenges facing higher education—including the work of the Committee on the Future of the American University.
Watch the full address for his reflections on moving forward together as a community.
Full prepared remarks: https://president.cornell.edu/public-remarks/2026-october-state-of-the-university-address/

entry.title: How does that manure get in our water?

media:group.media:title: How does that manure get in our water?
media:group.media:description:
That green scum on the lake in August? There's a real chance it started on a farm. Kirsten Workman, Cornell's nutrient management and environmental sustainability specialist, joins Research Matters to explain how manure — a valuable nutrient package when it stays put — becomes a public health hazard when it doesn't. From phosphorus indexes to injection versus spraying to the runoff forecast tool she built, this is a close look at the unglamorous, high-stakes science of keeping farm nutrients where they belong: in the soil, not the water supply.
Learn more about Kirsten Workman: https://cals.cornell.edu/people/kirsten-workman
Connect with Cornell research: https://www.cornell.edu/research/

entry.title: Who will take care of us when we're old?

media:group.media:title: Who will take care of us when we're old?
media:group.media:description:
America is aging faster than its systems are prepared for. In this two-guest conversation, Jenna Wells and Adriana Reyes bring their research to bear on the realities of eldercare today: who provides it, who pays for it, and what happens when both run short. It's a grounded, research-backed look at one of the biggest quiet crises facing families right now.
Learn more about Jenna Wells: https://human.cornell.edu/people/jenna-wells
Learn more about Adriana Reyes: https://publicpolicy.cornell.edu/people/adriana-reyes/
Connect with Cornell research: https://www.cornell.edu/research/

entry.title: What if buildings were made to be remade?

media:group.media:title: What if buildings were made to be remade?
media:group.media:description:
What if the building coming down next door could become the one going up down the street? Felix Heisel joins Research Matters to explain circular construction — the practice of designing buildings to be disassembled, reused, and reborn instead of landfilled. It's a rethink of how we build, one that could turn the construction industry's waste problem into its next resource.
Learn more about Felix Heisel: https://aap.cornell.edu/people/felix-heisel/
Connect with Cornell research: https://www.cornell.edu/research/

entry.title: Who gets to decide where free speech ends?

media:group.media:title: Who gets to decide where free speech ends?
media:group.media:description:
Free speech feels simple until you're the one drawing the lines. In this episode of Research Matters, Cornell's Gautam Hans unpacks the messy, high-stakes reality of civil liberties in America today, from campus speech fights to the digital platforms reshaping what "free expression" even means. It's a clear-eyed look at a right everyone claims to understand and almost no one agrees on.
Learn more about Gautam Hans: https://www.lawschool.cornell.edu/faculty-research/faculty-directory/gautam-hans/
Connect with Cornell research: https://www.cornell.edu/research/

entry.title: Why do we keep sabotaging our own best interests?

media:group.media:title: Why do we keep sabotaging our own best interests?
media:group.media:description:
Why do smart, capable people still blow off health screenings, hoard a bottle of wine "for a special occasion," and keep a box of college notebooks they'll never open again?
Cornell behavioral economist Suzanne Shu — a former electrical engineer turned behavioral economist — breaks down the psychology behind procrastination, overspending and our strange attachment to stuff. It's a funny, sharply researched look at why willpower isn't really the problem, and what actually helps.
Learn more about Suzanne Shu: https://business.cornell.edu/profiles/sbs78/
Connect with Cornell research: https://www.cornell.edu/research/

media:group.media:title: Deep connections drive psychedelic research
media:group.media:description: As psychedelic drugs gain more support from the medical community as a potential treatment for severe depression – and with the U.S. government relaxing its regulatory constraints – there remains a vast gap in understanding how the drugs work on the brain. Alex Kwan, Ph.D. ’09, professor of biomedical engineering in the Cornell Duffield College of Engineering, is at the center of a multidisciplinary investigation that is exploring the basic neurobiology and mechanics behind psychedelic compounds such as psilocybin.

entry.title: Taking a Leap of Faith: Cornell Outdoor Education

media:group.media:title: Taking a Leap of Faith: Cornell Outdoor Education
media:group.media:description:
Facing fears, pushing past mental blocks, and supporting one another—Cornell students conquer the high elements ropes course and prove that they can do what once felt impossible.
Through Cornell Outdoor Education (COE), students challenge themselves on the zip lines, thin log balances, and the ultimate "leap of faith." Watch as a group of students overcome their fear of heights, build trust, and turn a daunting obstacle into a bonding experience.

entry.title: How you can protect yourself from lingering wildfire smoke: A Cornell expert explains

media:group.media:title: How you can protect yourself from lingering wildfire smoke: A Cornell expert explains
media:group.media:description: Thanks to a heat dome and North American wildfires, smoke is blanketing communities in parts of the Northeast and Midwest — presenting health hazards. Alistair Hayden, assistant professor of practice in the Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine's Department of Public & Ecosystem Health, shares how you can protect yourself while the smoky haze lingers.

entry.title: Grape breeding at Cornell AgriTech: View from the vineyard

media:group.media:title: Grape breeding at Cornell AgriTech: View from the vineyard
media:group.media:description: Ever wonder what it takes to breed new grape varieties? Early summer is crossing season for Cornell AgriTech's Grapevine Breeding Program, a critical time for developing disease resistant, environmentally resilient, and high wine quality grapes. Madeline Oravec, assistant professor of grapevine breeding, genetics, and genomics, describes the process.

entry.title: How to protect your dog from Harmful Algal Blooms

media:group.media:title: How to protect your dog from Harmful Algal Blooms
media:group.media:description: In the warm months of spring, summer, and fall, Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) are a common and dangerous occurrence on lakes, ponds, and even backyard bird feeders. Water-loving dogs are particularly susceptible to the harms of HABs, but we can protect our pets — and enjoy the water with them — by following some key best practices, according to Dr. Aly Cohen, extension veterinarian at Cornell University's Riney Canine Health Center.

entry.title: Cornell President Kotlikoff's 2026 State of the University Address: Educating for Democracy

media:group.media:title: Cornell President Kotlikoff's 2026 State of the University Address: Educating for Democracy
media:group.media:description: In the annual State of the University address, Cornell President Michael I. Kotlikoff reflects on Cornell’s foundational history as the United States nears its 250th anniversary. Kotlikoff shares the value of a Cornell education and Cornell research, conveys the pressing challenges of the moment, and underscores the university's commitment to educating citizens that work across differences to build a better future – within an American democracy continually in progress.

entry.title: Cornell course introduces students to constructive disagreement

media:group.media:title: Cornell course introduces students to constructive disagreement
media:group.media:description:
Disagreement, a new class at Cornell co-developed by Arts and Sciences Dean Peter John Loewen, helps students learn how to confront and move through disagreements at work, at home, in their communities, and in society.
Watch a debate from Disagreement: https://youtu.be/Ef8I66D6gs0
Learn more about this class: https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/03/course-introduces-students-constructive-disagreement

entry.title: Jane Lynch delivers 2026 Senior Convocation address

media:group.media:title: Jane Lynch delivers 2026 Senior Convocation address
media:group.media:description:
On Thursday, May 21, Jane Lynch, MFA ’84, delivered the keynote address at the 2026 Senior Convocation inside Cornell's Barton Hall.
The Golden Globe and five-time Emmy Award winner, best known for her unforgettable roles in Glee, The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, Funny Girl, and Only Murders in the Building, returned to campus to celebrate this year's graduating class.

media:group.media:title: James Reinbold '26: A Cornell Story
media:group.media:description: Through his fusion of performance on the field and on the stage, a passion for storytelling and leadership drives James Reinbold ’26 to find his flow state. He bridges the gap between the brotherhood of the Cornell football team and the creative community of Performing and Media Arts—one play and one scene at a time. This is his Cornell story.
